document.title: On-demand glyph cache with DejaVu Sans fallback; Button font props
document.summary: TrueType and OpenType text now rasterises per glyph, at the exact Font Size, into shared atlas pages through stb_truetype. A character the requested Deck App Font lacks falls back to the Runtime Default Font. Button gains `font` and `fontSize`. This is slice 1 of three; CJK fallback and colour emoji come later.
document.why: Máté rejected a Latin-only glyph set and asked for full Unicode coverage including colour emoji. The approved design is a [dynamic glyph cache with fallback fonts](source:s1).

sources.title: Font glyph coverage
sources.gist: Revised proposal: dynamic glyph cache over stb_truetype, fallback fonts, Twemoji; shipped in three PRs. Slice 1 is the cache, call sites and Button props.

sources.label: feat(ui): draw text through the glyph cache with Runtime Default Font fallback
matemolnar8 on PR #90
sources.author: matemolnar8
sources.body: I would like the golden to contain an emoji and hungarian text. You can merge after that's added and verified.

lookFor: The [proposal](source:s1) uploads misses at the next frame start. Here `render_draw_list` caches every glyph the frame draws before `text_upload_pages`, so new text shows on its first frame. The first smoke run showed the lag as blank text.
The [proposal](source:s1) keys glyphs by font, glyph id and size, which leaves room for shaping. This change keys by `(font, size, codepoint)`, which is simpler while there is no shaping.

The [proposal](source:s1) moves the text calls in `shell.c` and `bootstrap.c` to `text_*`. Not done: the Shell and the failure screen still draw with raylib's built-in font, outside this slice's file ownership.
The [proposal](source:s1) treats DejaVu Sans as a fallback after the requested font. DejaVu Sans is already the Runtime Default Font, so the chain has two fonts and no second copy is vendored.
The [proposal](source:s1) feeds `.fnt`/`.bdf` fonts into the cache. Here they keep raylib's `DrawTextEx` path and get no fallback.
No kerning: pairs would cost a GPOS lookup per glyph pair on every per-frame measurement. Text keeps raylib's 1 px tracking, so line widths match the old layout.

The [proposal's](source:s1) smoke string `Újra 日本語 👍🏽` is not added. Per [Máté's review](source:s3) the smoke header draws Hungarian text with ő and ű plus 🎮, which is a `.notdef` box until slice 3; CJK waits for slice 2.

groups.title: stb_truetype v1.26
groups.why: raylib compiles its copy with `STBTT_STATIC` and installs no `external/` headers, so the cache needs its own copy.
groups.summary: `vendor/stb_truetype.h` is raylib 5.5's byte-for-byte copy; skip it.

groups.title: Glyph cache core
groups.why: The approved [design](source:s1) rasterises glyphs on first use at the exact size, with fallback fonts and capped atlas pages.
groups.summary: `glyph_cache_get` looks up `(font, size, codepoint)` in an stb_ds map and on a miss rasterises from the font or the fallback into a shelf-packed RGBA8 page, which `glyph_cache_harness` checks headlessly, including that every Hungarian letter is a real DejaVu Sans glyph.
lookFor: Perf: each page keeps a 4 MiB CPU mirror besides its 4 MiB texture, so the 4-page cap is 32 MiB worst case. The smoke app uses 1 page with 135 glyphs.

Subtle: when all pages are full and every page was used this frame, `atlas_allocate` refuses. The glyph returns `page = -1`, is not cached, and draws nothing until a later frame clears the least recently used page.
`glyph_font_load` rejects a font whose table directory points outside the file. stb_truetype still trusts the table contents, as it did under raylib.

groups.title: Text drawing through the cache
groups.why: Text, Button and TextInput must use the cache for fallback and exact-size glyphs ([commit](source:s2)).
groups.summary: `render.c` measures and draws through `text.c`, which takes `VdFont`s from the reworked `fonts.c` and uploads changed atlas pages once per frame after `cache_glyphs` warms them.
lookFor: Perf: `cache_glyphs` walks the whole tree every frame and measures each Text, Button label, TextInput value, placeholder and edit text once more before drawing.
Startup no longer bakes a 64 px atlas: `font_registry_init` only reads DejaVu Sans and calls `stbtt_InitFont`.
Switching packages calls `text_reset` from `unload_package_fonts`, which drops every cached glyph and atlas texture, Runtime Default Font glyphs included.
Line height now comes from font metrics (ascent + descent + line gap). DejaVu Sans has no line gap, so its lines keep their height; an author font with a line gap gets taller lines.

The golden changes because glyphs are sharper at exact size and advances are no longer floored at 64 px. Lines are a few pixels wider; sizes and baselines match. The smoke header now draws `Árvíztűrő tükörfúrógép 🎮` in its own `Rect`, because a Rect stacks each Text child one line below the previous one; the emoji draws as DejaVu Sans's `.notdef` box until the colour emoji slice.

groups.title: Button font and fontSize
groups.why: The [design](source:s1) gives Button the font props Text already has.
groups.summary: `VitaButtonProps` gains `font`/`fontSize`, the reconciler passes them after the label, and `read_button_props` stores the font name that `render_button_instance` draws with.
lookFor: Breaking (internal): the native Button now takes 22 arguments, with the font name at index 10. A `runtime.js` from before this change makes every Button create and update return early. The runtime and host ship together.
An unset `fontSize` now passes 0 and the host applies `VD_BUTTON_FONT_SIZE_DEFAULT` (20), where the reconciler used to hard-code 20.

groups.title: Glossary and SDK README
groups.why: AGENTS.md asks for in-place doc fixes when behaviour changes; per-character fallback is new author-visible behaviour.
groups.summary: The **Deck App Font** and **Runtime Default Font** entries, and one SDK README paragraph, describe the fallback and the Button font props.

commits.subject: test(smoke): Hungarian and emoji line in the golden
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The smoke header draws "Árvíztűrő tükörfúrógép 🎮", so the golden covers
ő and ű (outside Latin-1) through the glyph cache. The emoji is the
.notdef box until the colour emoji slice. The glyph cache harness checks
every Hungarian letter resolves to a real DejaVu Sans glyph.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(ui): draw text through the glyph cache with Runtime Default Font fallback
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
TrueType and OpenType fonts load as font bytes instead of a pre-baked 64 px atlas, so startup does no rasterising. Text, Button and TextInput measure and draw through text.c; each frame caches the glyphs it draws, then uploads changed atlas pages once before drawing, because vitaGL copies a whole texture that changes after it was drawn. .fnt and .bdf fonts keep raylib's path. Word-wrap chunking no longer splits a UTF-8 sequence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(ui): on-demand glyph cache over stb_truetype
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Glyphs rasterise at the exact pixel size on first use, keyed by (font, size, codepoint), into 1024x1024 RGBA8 atlas pages (4 MiB, at most 4). When every page is full, the least recently used one not used this frame is cleared. A codepoint the font lacks comes from the fallback font, else the font's .notdef.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Máté Molnár

raylib builds its copy with STBTT_STATIC and installs no external headers, so the glyph cache needs its own.
